pr_body:
Fixes #18140

Part of #18242

- `GET /api/v1/admin/domain_blocks` lists domain blocks
- `GET /api/v1/admin/domain_blocks/:id` shows one by ID
- `DELETE /api/v1/admin/domain_blocks/:id` deletes a given domain block
- `POST /api/v1/admin/domain_blocks` to create a new domain block:
  if it conflicts with an existing one, returns an error with an attribute `existing_domain_block` with the rendered domain block

Note that there is no API to search for a domain block given a domain yet.

___

issue_context.title: Add the ability for an admin to manage domain blocks via API
issue_context.body:
### Pitch

As an admin, I would like to be able to manage domain blocks via API for my instance similar to how I manage accounts and reports. 

### Motivation

Blocking via UI can be slow. I would like to be able to block multiple instances at once or at least be able to script such an action for myself. 

Right now I can handle almost all other moderation aspects outside of the app and be alerted when I need to take action and take it by using just the api and some custom script for my instance. This makes moderation a lot easier. However, domain blocks can’t be managed this way. 

So, admins would benefit from being able to write their own tools and users would benefit from a happier admin able to respond to things more efficiently :).
comments:
This would be incredibly nice, because right now I have to give my utility scripts a username and password so it can authenticate and run with session cookies.

The script I use the most just allows me to pass a domain and one of a couple predefined reasons, and it will block it and make sure the publicly listed reason is one of the correct ones - if anyone wants more motivation.
@ClearlyClaire this is such good news!! I've been running my instance since 2017 and this has been a constant struggle so I'm so looking forward to it.
Can you have a look at #18247 and see if that would address your concerns? I initially planned to do that as part of a larger admin API work effort but I figured this can be done separately.
Yes, that would do it. Thank you, this will be super helpful.

review_comments: This is the first multi-word OAuth scope. Should we go with underscores here or use dashes?

This is a completely new API design, we have never used custom error serializers before. However, I believe there might be a more generalized validation errors rendering system that I added for the sign-up API, perhaps it could be reused?

I am not sure how useful it would be. Here, we're specifically interested in knowing *which* domain block it conflicts with so that the client app can show it on conflict. I am not completely sure how that would fit.

I think it would probably be acceptable to simply return a conflict error here and let the API user decide to update the existing block instead. My concern is duplication of non-straightforward logic between controllers.
